title: r-Way Birthday Collision Threshold Scaling (OQ-02-OQ-03)
description: Extends birthday collision asymptotics to r-way collisions. Defines the r-tuple collision expectation C(n,r)/d^(r-1), proves upper and lower bounds via Mathlib's choose inequalities, and characterizes the threshold: collisions are expected when (r!)·d^(r-1) < (n+1-r)^r, giving the d^((r-1)/r) scaling.

meta.author: Classical (generalized birthday problem), formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib
originalContributions: Classical recovery: r=2 reduces to pairwise collision count
Upper and lower bounds on expectation via Mathlib choose inequalities
meta.assumptions: None (0 axioms). All results fully proved from Mathlib.

overview.problemStatement: OQ-02-OQ-03: Can the tight collision asymptotics (pairwise case) be extended to r-way collisions, where the threshold scales as d^((r-1)/r)?
overview.text: Extends birthday collision asymptotics to r-way collisions using combinatorial counting bounds.
overview.proofStrategy: Define C(n,r)/d^(r-1) as the expected number of birthday-sharing r-tuples. Use Mathlib's Nat.choose_le_pow and Nat.pow_le_choose to bound this quantity, then characterize when it exceeds 1.
keyInsights: The r-tuple collision expectation C(n,r)/d^(r-1) generalizes the pairwise count n(n-1)/(2d)
Mathlib provides tight bounds: (n+1-r)^r/r! ≤ C(n,r) ≤ n^r/r!
Setting C(n,r)/d^(r-1) = 1 gives the threshold n ≈ (r!·d^(r-1))^(1/r) ≈ d^((r-1)/r)
The full exponential bound requires Poisson approximation (future work)
